content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the gross structure of the kidney
Identify the main regions of the kidney
Describe the structure of a nephron
Explain how the structure of the nephron relates to its function

are the main excretory organs in humans. They filter blood, remove waste products, and regulate water and salt balance. Understanding kidney structure helps explain how these vital functions are carried out.
One on each side of spine
Kidneys receive about 25% of cardiac output!
Tube carrying urine from kidney to bladder
Tube carrying urine out of body
Around loop of Henle; maintains gradient
The kidney makes urine directly from blood
Blood is filtered, then useful substances reabsorbed
Urine is stored in the kidneys
Urine is stored in the bladder
Each kidney has about 1 million nephrons
All parts of the nephron are in the medulla
Some parts are in cortex, some in medulla
Kidneys receive blood via renal artery, remove waste, return via renal vein
Nephron = functional unit (~1 million per kidney)
Nephron parts: Bowman's capsule, PCT, loop of Henle, DCT, collecting duct
Glomerulus: knot of capillaries where filtration occurs
Different parts of nephron have different functions
Cells adapted with microvilli, mitochondria for reabsorption
